function: Deep-unfolded alternating projected gradient network (PNAPG-Net) jointly designs BS active beamforming and passive phase shifts of multiple RISs to maximize multicast sum spectral efficiency (pp. 3, 6-7).
system: Downlink multi-group multicast: BS with 8-antenna ULA, two passive RISs with 100 elements each, 4 single-antenna users in 2 groups, 2 GHz carrier, 180 kHz bandwidth (pp. 3, 9).
method: Model-driven deep unfolding of alternating projected gradient with trainable step sizes (20 layers), trained with negative sum-SE loss and no labels; pyramid segment-wise training (pp. 6-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh BS-user, Ricean BS-RIS and RIS-user links, path loss set following 3GPP; 1,000 training and 1,000 testing LoS samples, random user locations (pp. 9-10).
test_conditions: Ricean training and testing (Pt=10 dBm, 100 elements per RIS, 2 groups); mismatch tests with other Pt, elements, groups, Rayleigh channel; imperfect-CSI NMSE sweep (pp. 12-13).
baselines: Non-learned: MM [27] and APG [28] algorithms, random passive beamforming, Monte-Carlo upper bound. Learned: only NAPG-Net, the same network trained directly (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency (bps/Hz), iterations to converge, runtime in seconds, performance degradation under training-testing mismatch (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Per-iteration complexity O(GKNM) versus APG and MM orders (Table II, pp. 10-11); runtime 0.0311 s versus APG 0.1572 s and MM 109.4346 s (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 9: "the pathlosses are set following the 3GPP propagation environment"; only the path loss follows 3GPP, fading is Rayleigh and Ricean in a custom simulator, and no 3GPP fading model, DeepMIMO or measurement is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "we test the performance of the PNAPG-Net with the parameters S trained at different maximum transmit power"; p. 12: "the deterioration is less than 0.2% for the mismatched PNAPG-Net" with other RIS element numbers; Rayleigh and Ricean training are also crossed.
q3_support: p. 10: "against the benchmark algorithms, including the MM algorithm [27] and the APG algorithm [28]" (both non-learned); p. 11: "a method referred to as NAPG-Net, which directly trains all trainable parameters" is the same network trained differently, so no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "the PNAPG-Net algorithm uses the step sizes trained before, resulting in a per-iteration complexity" of O(GKNM); Table II on p. 11 gives complexity orders and runtimes.
q5_support: p. 10: "The training and testing datasets each contain 1,000 LoS component samples" generated by the authors' simulator; no code link, DOI or public dataset is given.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Deep unfolding with trainable step sizes counts as learned; area 3 (joint active and passive beamforming with multiple RISs). q1 is 0 because only the path loss follows 3GPP (TS 36.814 via [45], [46]) and the fading is Rayleigh and Ricean. q3 is 0 because NAPG-Net and the single-RIS and active-only versions are variants of the proposed network. Tables I and II were read from the page images (pp. 10-11).
